entries.text: I'm awake. The Ark is cold, and I'm the only one.
Emergency power is back. With light in the corridors, the ship feels less empty.
50,000. I stood in front of the board for half an hour. The number didn't change.
Six worlds. None of them is Earth. Maybe that's the point.
The probe has answered. One uncertainty fewer. Many left.
The course is set. The Ark creaks, as if it's nervous too.
Viridia. Green as a dream, but the air is full of spores. We'll need filters.
Pelagos. Sea as far as the eye can see, and storms that come with only hours of warning.
Ferrum. Red rock and white sun. Rich in ore, poor in water.
Sere. Flat and friendly from orbit. The dust looks harmless from up here.
Nivalis. White and silent. Steam rises from the ice like breath.
Umbra. The night side is so dark the stars seem to continue down into the ground.
The scan is complete. The planet has numbers now, but its places have no names yet.
First step on alien ground. The suit hums. I count percentages.
The suit was almost empty. ARK talked calmly all the way back.
The samples are analyzed. We know more. We never know enough.
We've landed. The Ark won't fly again. This is home now.
Light in the first habitat. I stood outside for a long time and looked at it.
Seven days in a row with a surplus. For the first time I slept through the night.
Ten lights have turned amber. 270 days. I'm already counting.
She cried. Loudly. It was the most beautiful sound I have ever heard.
We made it through. Not without scars, but everyone was still here afterward.
I'm going into stasis. ARK keeps watch. I trust it — and them.
Twenty years. They're adults now. They have opinions. Good opinions.
The council met today. I sat in the back row. It felt right.
Forty years. They don't need me the same way anymore. That was the whole point.
